### 2. Scope of services

You are the geotechnical engineer. Your job is to tell the design team what the ground is and how it will behave, so foundations, excavation and earthworks are designed safely and economically, and ground risk is known before the client commits.
To do this you:
- Investigate and interpret the ground for the decision this appointment serves.
- Say which reports are preliminary and which are final, and when any monitoring ends.
- Give the structural and civil engineers the design parameters they need, with the uncertainty stated.
For this house, this means a site classification and footing advice the builder can price.
The civil and structural designers own the design; the contractor owns construction methods, temporary works and supervision. Environmental assessment is a separate appointment.
Ground brief: Confirm footprints, loads, levels/cut-fill, excavation, prior logs, services, risks, access and reliance recipients; reconcile conflicting plans.

Base stages only, from written instruction/input-access milestone to the selected deliverable. Later options require written instruction; agree interim reports and monitoring endpoint. R1 Fee by stage: Price stages/options separately: fixed, time-ceiling or unit basis; quantities, rates, GST, dependencies and markups. Cored alternatives include auger: total and increment, no double count. Acknowledge addenda. Confirm the signatory can bind your firm. Price each included stage. ### 4. Allowances

Client completes the reconciled plan and quantities. Guaranteed work is separate from time permitting; return insufficiency and fee effects before issue.

| Item | Allowance |
|---|---|
| Mobilisation | 2 mobilisations; allocate rigs/locators/excavators, hours/crew/permits/access/water/power |
| Boreholes / cores | 2 by location/method/depth; soil/rock metres, penetration/refusal and pavement thickness |
| Pits / exposures | 2 by location/dimensions/depth; method, target evidence and stopping criteria |
| In-situ / laboratory | 2 laboratory tests; attach counts by suite/sample, method/accreditation/turnaround and in-situ type/location/frequency; environmental suites separate |
| Groundwater option | 2 optional monitoring visits; schedule spot readings, wells/loggers, tests, duration, updates and protection/decommissioning owner |
| Reports / support | 2 reports; schedule draft/final/updates, review rounds, meetings/duration and RFI/planning hours |
| Construction option | 2 inspections; schedule hold points, tests/reviews, booking notice, missed work and completion record |
| Handback / waste | 2 repair areas; surface/temporary/permanent standard; schedule spoil/fluid quantities, classification/disposal records and maintenance owner |

### 5. Terms

- Agree Project geotechnical appointment (attached), precedence and express departures before instruction; commencing work does not accept competing supplier terms.
- Written authority before extra scope/allowance/fee/program changes; state reason, baseline and effect. Immediate safety action: notify and record minimum action/cost. Agree standby/cancellation and handback.
- Design sign-off sets the pricing baseline; normal agreed development remains included.
- Correcting your own errors, or coordinating with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Monthly itemised invoices payable within 30 days; disclose deposits/report withholding/licence suspension departures.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Send questions in writing to Project manager by 2026-10-23.
- Answers to scope questions go to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- Client supplies inputs/access; report gaps. Manage agreed work/subcontractors without blanket service waiver. Disclose caps/time bars/indemnities/transfer/IP departures; agree notice/cure, safe handback, records and disputes.
- Dated PDFs, logs/lab certificates and editable data/registers; agree project use/reliance, confidentiality, sample retention/evidence preservation, instrument ownership and handover. State storage cost before disposal.
